learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how assets lose value over time, and learn how businesses safely lock away profits today for unknown emergencies tomorrow!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: When you buy a car, its value drops every year due to wear and tear, passage of time, or new technology (obsolescence). Depreciation is accounting's way of spreading the cost of an asset over its useful life.

Straight Line Method (SLM): Depreciation is a fixed amount every year based on original cost. Written Down Value (WDV): Depreciation is calculated on the remaining (reduced) book value every year, so the amount gets smaller.
A provision is money set aside for a KNOWN future liability, but the exact amount is unknown (e.g., Provision for Doubtful Debts). It must be recorded even if the company makes a loss.
A reserve is a portion of profit kept aside to strengthen the financial position or for future expansion (like a savings account). It is only created if the company actually makes a profit.

fun_activity.title: 📱 The Smartphone Depreciation
fun_activity.instructions: Did you buy a phone for ₹20,000? Assuming it lasts 4 years and will be worth zero at the end. Use the Straight Line Method: ₹20,000 / 4 years = ₹5,000. Your phone costs you ₹5,000 in depreciation every single year!

exam_tips: 📌 Formula for SLM Depreciation: $(Original Cost - Scrap Value) / Estimated Useful Life$.
📌 Amortization applies to Intangible assets (patents, software), Depletion applies to Natural resources (coal mines), and Depreciation applies to Tangible assets (machinery).
📌 Difference between Provision and Reserve is heavily tested: Provision is a 'Charge' (mandatory), Reserve is an 'Appropriation' (optional out of profits).
quick_recap: ⭐ Depreciation allocates the cost of a fixed asset over its useful life to match expenses with revenues.
⭐ SLM charges equal depreciation yearly; WDV charges higher depreciation in early years.
⭐ Provisions are for known liabilities; Reserves are retained earnings for future growth.
